**Explanation (80 words):**
After White's king moved to e4, it's attacking your pieces but the rook on a7 is undefended. The key is f5+—this check lures the king away from defending its rook. No matter where the king goes (Kxf5, Ke5, or Kd5), your rook on g7 can capture on a7, winning a full piece. This tactical pattern—forcing a piece to an even worse square with check—shows why you must always check if forcing moves create new weaknesses in your opponent's position.
